summary: Compare two instructor-assigned rectangular hollow steel armatures for bending strength, self-weight, and cantilever tip deflection in a simplified museum-tail support model.

problemStatement:
You are assisting a museum exhibit engineering team preparing a mounted sauropod skeleton. For a preliminary Mechanics of Materials assessment, a tail-support segment is represented as a straight horizontal steel cantilever of length {{armature_L_m}} {{armature_L_m_unit}}, rigidly fixed to an equivalent pelvis-region mounting frame.

The supported exhibit elements apply an instructor-assigned uniform downward load of {{armature_we_N_m}} {{armature_we_N_m_unit}}, excluding the steel armature's self-weight. Compare two instructor-assigned rectangular hollow sections. Candidate A is {{armature_HA_mm}} × {{armature_BA_mm}} × {{armature_tnomA_mm}} mm nominal; Candidate B is {{armature_HB_mm}} × {{armature_BB_mm}} × {{armature_tnomB_mm}} mm nominal. Use the simplified sharp-corner design thickness t = {{armature_t_factor}}tnom. These are teaching geometries, not dimensions inferred from the photograph or verified stocked products.
engineeringGoal: Determine which candidate, if either, fits within the assigned concealment envelope, meets the minimum bending-yield factor of safety, and limits downward free-end deflection to the assigned value after including steel self-weight. Identify the governing response and make a preliminary mechanics-based recommendation without presenting it as certification of a museum installation.
